quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should you wear to reduce serious injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: A helmet is your best protection in a crash. A plastic face shield that does not break easily will protect your face from injury.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, how far behind the vehicle ahead should a motorcyclist stay?
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. Use a larger distance if conditions are poor.

questions.question: What should you do when lights flash at a railroad crossing sign?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Turn around and find an alternate route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at a flashing railroad crossing sign. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before going. Never try to beat a train.

questions.question: Where are you most likely to have a conflict with other vehicles?
questions.explanation: Most conflicts happen at intersections. The biggest danger is when cars turn left in front of motorcycles.

questions.question: What road surface may have poor traction?
questions.explanation: Poor traction can happen on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement, gravel roads, lane markings, steel plates, and utility hole covers.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on good pavement, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you have stopped completely.
Release the rear brake and only use the front brake.
Release the rear brake and then quickly re-apply the brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you have stopped completely.
questions.explanation: Keep the rear wheel locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle if it is upright and going straight, even with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the road with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle begins moving again.
Merge into a lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge into a lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: Move to a different lane to give the emergency vehicle space. Slow down and be ready to stop. Give emergency vehicles, tow trucks, and roadside help vehicles extra room.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, does a motorcycle stop and speed up differently?

options.text: Less time than usual to stop and speed up.
The same amount of time to stop and speed up as it usually does.
More time than usual to stop and speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: More time than usual to stop and speed up.
questions.explanation: Extra weight slows acceleration and deceleration. Your motorcycle responds more slowly with a passenger than when you ride alone.

questions.question: What should you do if you get a flat tire while riding?

options.text: Hold the handle grips firmly and stay off the brakes.
Shift your weight toward the good wheel and brake normally.
Brake on the good wheel while immediately pulling off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handle grips firmly and stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly and keep your motorcycle straight. Only brake if you know which tire is flat. Leave the road once you have slowed down enough.

questions.question: How should a passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: Put their feet on the ground when the motorcycle is stopped.
Not ride without a back rest.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the operator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the operator.
questions.explanation: A passenger should sit forward without crowding the driver. Keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: If you wear a jacket for protection while riding in hot weather, you should:

options.text: Take frequent breaks to cool off.
Remove the jacket to stay cool in the sun.
Keep the jacket on to protect you from the heat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the jacket on to protect you from the heat.
questions.explanation: A good riding jacket protects you from crashes no matter the weather. Jackets also help prevent dehydration in hot weather. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you from overheating.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to tell the other vehicle to go.
Drive through the intersection and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: Who must wear a helmet on a moving motorcycle?
questions.explanation: All riders and passengers must wear a helmet when riding a motorcycle, motor-driven cycle, or motorized bicycle.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should generally form a:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. It keeps riders close together while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file when turning, taking curves, entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: Why should a motorcyclist not rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Mirrors can get dirty and limit your view.

questions.explanation: You cannot rely only on mirrors to stay aware of your surroundings. Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, where should you position your motorcycle in your lane?
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This gives you a better view ahead and helps drivers in the next lane see your intention to pass.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on a straight road, what happens?

options.text: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
You will likely lose control of the motorcycle.
You must release the rear brake to regain control.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can usually control your motorcycle if it is upright and traveling straight, even with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, where should you ride in your lane?
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass another vehicle on the left.

questions.question: A motorcycle must have all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: In Wyoming, motorcycles must have at least one headlight, one taillight, one brake light, one red rear reflector, a left mirror, a muffler, and a horn. Turn signals are not required.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: The driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You will have more escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. The driver may not see you in their blind spot. Also, the vehicle could block your way to escape if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding?
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing to be more visible. This helps during day and night. Reflective materials also make you easier to see.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How quickly the alcohol is consumed
How often the person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: BAC depends on body weight, how much alcohol you drink, and how fast you drink it. How often you drink does not affect your BAC. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more time to stop, when you cannot see clearly, or when traffic is heavy. Rain makes it harder to stop quickly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that the road will divide ahead.
